source.publication: 2025 Tax Rate Table (Tax Look Up Table); 2025 PIT-1 Personal Income Tax Return Instructions
source.section: Tax Rate Table PDF pages 1 to 6, rows; PDF page 7 (T-7), over 100,000; Form PIT-1 lines 9 to 18 and 22; instructions PDF page 25, line 12

worked: Federal (given, not tested): federal AGI = wages (person 0) 215,750.00 = 215,750.00. Federal taxable income = 215,750.00 - standard deduction 15,750.00 = 200,000.00 (federal senior deduction ignored; Form PIT-1 takes only the federal line 12 amount, and no line for what the federal return subtracts after line 12). Form PIT-1, married filing separately. Line 9 federal AGI 215,750.00. Line 10 0.00 (standard deduction taken). Line 11 additions 0.00. Line 12 federal standard deduction 15,750.00. Line 13 dependents 0.00. Line 14 0.00: federal AGI 215,750.00 is over the worksheet's printed ceiling 27,500.00 for this status, so the worksheet is not completed. Line 15 PIT-ADJ deductions and exemptions 0.00. Line 17 = 215,750.00 + 0.00 - 15,750.00 - 0.00 - 0.00 = 200,000.00. By the projection: state_agi = federal taxable income 200,000.00 = 200,000.00; less base deductions 0.00 gives 200,000.00. Line 18 tax, schedule as numbers: 1.5% x 4,000.00 = 60 + 3.2% x 8,500.00 = 272 + 4.3% x 12,500.00 = 537.5 + 4.7% x 25,000.00 = 1,175 + 4.9% x 107,500.00 = 5,267.5 + 5.9% x 42,500.00 = 2,507.5; total 9,819.5, to the cent 9,819.50. The printed section on T-7 gives 9,817.50; expected keeps the schedule figure 9,819.50, 2.00 more. Lines 19 to 21 0.00. Line 22 net New Mexico income tax 9,819.50. Above 157,500 the gap to the printed section is 2.00, not the 2.50 of the 4.9% band, because T-7 prints 7,310 where 4,492 + 4.9% of 57,500 is 7,309.50.
accepted_approximations: Over 100,000 the printed section is base plus rate, and each base is the table's last row (midpoint 99,950), not the tax at 100,000. A bracket schedule cannot hold that step down, so the schedule gives more than the printed section at every income over 100,000.
